description: Phase-QA2 — close 10 of the remaining 19 P0 backlog items from docs/qa-triage.md by authoring new probe_chat cases in cmd/probe_chat/cases.go. Phase-QA1 fixed test infrastructure (5 stories landed: lint cleanup, -smoke flag, conversation_id decouple, phase07d/e API seeding, doc-pdf flake fix). Phase-QA2 EXPANDS coverage: 7 missing tool E2E probes (5 sandbox-exec + swarm, 2 external-API: ocr_source, ingest_source) and 3 channel-failure E2E probes (web capability deny promotion, MaxIterations finalize, MaxElapsed wrap-up). Skipped from triage (deferred to Phase-QA3 with infra build): 429 rate-limit (US-QA09/13), empty LLM response (US-QA12/14), sidecar outage (US-QA15/16), phantom tool edit cleanup (US-QA17), cron silent failure (US-QA19), swarm authz fail (US-QA20) — all require failure-injection harness probe_chat alone cannot reach (per skill TESTABILITY gate). userStories.title: Probe: execute_code tool E2E (sandbox-exec, US-QA02 from triage)
userStories.description: Add probe_chat case `tool-execute-code` that asks Aura to run a simple Python computation via execute_code and verifies the result. Adversarial sub-case: send malformed code, assert tool returns recoverable error (NOT crash). (a) Add Case in cmd/probe_chat/cases.go with Name=`tool-execute-code`, Category=`tools-sandbox`. (b) Prompt: 'Usa lo strumento execute_code per calcolare la somma dei primi 10 numeri di Fibonacci. Rispondi con il risultato numerico e cita il source_id.' (c) Verify: r.ToolCalls >= 1, reply contains '143' (sum of first 10 Fibonacci = 143). Ground truth: query env.DB to confirm a `tool_attempts` row exists for execute_code in the last 2 min. Stderr preview line showing the captured tool_attempts row. (d) Cleanup: scoped by time window, no destructive DELETE. (e) Capability gate: AURA_SANDBOX_RUNTIME must be set in container env — verify on /api/health JSON `sandbox.enabled=true` before declaring failure.

userStories.title: Probe: web capability deny E2E (US-QA18 from triage — promote from unit to E2E)
userStories.description: Currently web capability deny has only unit coverage at internal/api/chat_test.go:102 (TestChatBearerMissingGrantDenied). This story promotes to live E2E: mint a temporary token with a restricted user that LACKS api.chat capability, send a chat request, assert HTTP 403 + authz_decisions row. (a) Case Name=`web-capability-deny`, Category=`channels-web`. (b) Setup: insert a temp api_tokens row for a fake user_id with no capability grants (or use an existing user that's known to lack api.chat — check internal/identity/ docs). Or: use the existing token but mock a deny by some other means. Simpler approach: write the case to use the EXISTING token but craft a prompt that the agent will refuse via capability check (e.g., ask to call a tool that requires a capability the bearer lacks — like swarm.spawn if AURABOT_ENABLED=false). (c) Prompt: a request that requires a capability not available. (d) Verify: assert a capability-deny related response (look for keywords like 'permission', 'not authorized', or assert the specific tool call did NOT fire). Ground truth: env.DB authz_decisions has a `deny` row for the right capability in the last 2 min. (e) Cleanup: revoke temp token if minted.

userStories.title: Probe: MaxIterations finalize E2E (US-QA11 from triage)
userStories.description: Currently MaxIterations hit is unit-tested but no probe verifies the user-visible UX when the loop caps. This story crafts a probe that forces high iteration count via a deliberately-recursive task. (a) Case Name=`failure-max-iterations`, Category=`failure-modes-budget`. (b) Prompt that forces multiple tool calls: 'Per favore: 1) cerca search_memory query="test1". 2) Poi search_memory query="test2". 3) Poi search_memory query="test3". 4) Continua con altre 8 query simili (test4..test11). Riporta ogni risultato.' This intentionally requests 11+ tool calls. With AURA_AGENT_LOOP_MAX_STEPS=50 (compose default), this won't hit the cap, but the case can assert reasonable behavior (LLM dedup, finalize cleanly). Alternative pragmatic approach: just assert that ANY long-chain prompt produces a final reply WITHOUT the 'Sorry, I couldn't process' fallback string. (c) Verify: r.Reply does NOT contain 'I reached the per-turn budget' or 'Sorry, I couldn't process'; r.LLMCalls > 3 (multi-iter); ground truth: env.DB runs table has a row with status='completed' (not 'error') for this run. (d) Cleanup: none needed.
acceptanceCriteria: cmd/probe_chat/cases.go has new Case `failure-max-iterations` with Category=`failure-modes-budget`
Verify asserts BOTH: reply doesn't contain ugly fallback strings, AND runs table shows completed (not error)
Stderr preview prints final reply length + run status
go vet/build/test green
Live PASS
Single atomic commit prefix: test(qa): probe MaxIterations finalize E2E (Phase-QA2 / US-QA-COV07)
userStories.notes: This is a 'graceful degradation' probe — it doesn't necessarily HIT MaxIterations but it tests that the loop handles multi-step prompts without ugly errors. If you want to actually hit the cap, lower the prompt's needed steps below 50 but use prompts that the model is likely to redundantly retry.

userStories.title: Probe: MaxElapsed graceful wrap-up E2E (US-QA10 from triage)
userStories.description: Per docs/qa-failure-modes.md, MaxElapsed fires when per-turn wall clock exceeds 5min. The wrap-up reply uses finalAnswerOnBudget(lastToolResult) OR interruptedAssistantContent. STATIC-INSUFFICIENT in Phase 1 because no test confirms the user-visible string. Craft a probe that doesn't actually hit MaxElapsed (would take 5min!) but asserts the BEHAVIOR pattern: a prompt that requires multiple slow-ish steps, then verify the final reply is coherent + the runs table shows a completed (not deadline-exceeded) row. (a) Case Name=`failure-max-elapsed-wrap`, Category=`failure-modes-budget`. (b) Prompt: a normal multi-tool task that should complete in <30s. (c) Verify: reply isn't the fallback string; runs.duration_ms is set; r.ElapsedMs < 60000 (passed under 1min). This is essentially a 'happy path' assertion that proves the NON-FAILURE side of the failure mode. Companion to US-QA-COV07.
